PASS with two caveats, both about the TEXT rather than the mapping. (1) EESR_1 ships BLANK item_text. The PLOS S1 workbook is a wjx-style survey export in which the first sub-item column of each matrix question carries the question STEM instead of that sub-item's own label: column 5 (1-based) reads 'When you have the following emotions, the degree of desire to eat is', and columns 6-27 read '@10. <emotion>'. data/yang_2023_emotional_eating.py builds ees_cols as [that stem column] + [the 22 '@10' columns] and assigns EESR_1..EESR_23 positionally, so EESR_1 is a real item whose emotion word the deposit does not preserve. The stem is shipped as `instructions`; EESR_1's item_text is left blank rather than guessed. 22 of 23 items carry wording. (2) The deposit's English collapses two pairs of distinct items onto IDENTICAL labels -- EESR_5 and EESR_20 both read 'hostile', EESR_13 and EESR_22 both read 'depressed'. These are four distinct columns with four distinct response distributions (means 2.310/2.279 and 2.688/2.565), so they are distinct Chinese emotion words that the workbook's English rendering does not distinguish. Their item CODES are verified exactly; their English text cannot be told apart. (3) option_text is blank for all five levels: the paper states only 'Responses ranged from 1 to 5, with 1 representing a total lack of these emotions and 5 indicating a high degree of emotion', which is a description of the endpoints in the Measures section, not the administered anchor wording, and no anchor labels appear anywhere in the deposit. Nothing was padded with its own scale number. AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED (audit_batch.R: '4.3% of rows have blank item_text | 100% of rows have blank option_text'). Both are expected and are ITEMTEXT GAPS IN THE SOURCE, not defects in the response data and not extraction errors. The 4.3% is exactly EESR_1 (1 of 23 items x 5 resp levels = 5 of 115 rows), whose emotion label the deposit replaced with the matrix stem, per caveat (1) above. The 100% blank option_text is caveat (3): the deposit carries no value labels and the paper gives only endpoint descriptions, so nothing could be shipped without padding. The response data itself is complete and well formed -- all 23 items use all five levels.
